title: Standing against all hatred
hook: every person is in the image of God
tomorrow: Owen and Yasmin both came to the cast party. what does each keep?

segments.voice: Two weeks of community and justice, and this week's lines: pay today, the land is shared, animals feel, no stumbling blocks, asking for help is holy. Yesterday's: stand together, and one life weighs a whole world.

Closing night. The cast bows, and backstage someone does an impression of the new girl's accent. People laugh. It isn't about Jews this time. So is it still your fight? The Torah's answer starts on its first page, in the JPS 1917 translation: "And God created man in His own image, in the image of God created He him."
screen: `CLOSING NIGHT, BACKSTAGE.` → `NOT ABOUT JEWS THIS TIME.` → `"IN THE IMAGE OF GOD."`

segments.voice: Not one people, not one family: the first human, ancestor of everyone. The Mishnah asks why the Torah begins with a single person, and gives reasons. One is for the sake of peace, so no one could ever say to another, my ancestor was greater than yours. Everyone shares the same one. Another is a picture. A king stamps many coins with one seal, and they all come out alike. God stamped every human with the seal of the first, and not one comes out like another. One human family, and no copies. In the Sifra, Rabbi Akiva calls love your neighbor as yourself a great principle of the Torah. Ben Azzai names a greater one: this is the book of the generations of Adam. Why greater? A neighbor can be narrowed to people like you. Adam can't. So standing against all hatred is yesterday's lesson, widened. A slur about someone's accent, skin, faith or body forgets the seal. Lived, it's the same calm skill: name it, stand beside the person, and don't wait until you're the target. Something to tell a friend tonight: the Mishnah says humanity started with one person so nobody could brag about their ancestors.
screen: `ONE FIRST HUMAN, FOR EVERYONE.` · `NO ANCESTOR IS GREATER.` · `ONE SEAL, NO COPIES.` · `THE BOOK OF THE GENERATIONS OF ADAM.` · then, large: `EVERY IMAGE.`

segments.voice: Stand up, feet planted, the way you'd stand next to someone being mocked: not in front of them, beside them. Let your shoulders settle level, as if theirs were right there. Hold it for a few breaths, and bring to mind one person who might need someone beside them this week.
screen: `STAND UP.` · `BESIDE, NOT IN FRONT.` · `ONE PERSON THIS WEEK.`

segments.voice: Standing against all hatred: refusing to forget that every person carries the image of God, one human family with no copies.
Keep it near: every image, every face, and one first ancestor for all of us. Two weeks, done.

howItsDone: Many Jewish communities teach that every person is created in God's image, b'tzelem Elohim, and join interfaith and neighborhood efforts against every kind of hatred, not only antisemitism.

chat.meaning: The Mishnah says everyone shares one ancestor, so no one can say theirs is greater. Every person bears God's image; standing up isn't only for your own group.

Mishnah.meaning: the early book of Jewish law the rabbis built on

Sifra.meaning: an early rabbinic commentary on Leviticus

Akiva.meaning: a rabbi of the Mishnah's time, teacher of many students

Ben Azzai.meaning: a sage who named humanity's shared origin a greater principle

sources.quoted: And God created man in His own image, in the image of God created He him

Sifra, Kedoshim 4:12 (Akiva: love your neighbor is a great principle; Ben Azzai: 'this is the book of the generations of Adam', Genesis 5:1, is greater)
